title: Simple-reflection integral Gauss chart with positive-system support
statement:
Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ be a finite reduced root datum with $\mathbf Q\Phi=M\otimes\mathbf Q$ and $\mathbf Z\Phi^\vee=M^\vee$, and $(G,T_{\mathbf Q}=D_{\mathbf Q}(M))$ a split rational realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Fix a base $\Delta$, rational root parameters $p_\alpha$, orderings and integral one-sign groups $E_\pm$ satisfying [lem-sfb-rational-chevalley-one-sign-integrality]. Thus $E_\pm$ are affine spaces over $\mathbf Z$ with polynomial group laws, their generic fibres are the ordered root-product unipotent radicals, and $T_{\mathbf Z}=D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$ acts by the root characters [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Set $C=E_-\times_{\mathbf Z}T_{\mathbf Z}\times_{\mathbf Z}E_+$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with coordinate inclusions of $E_-$, $T_{\mathbf Z}$ and $E_+$. Suppose the ordered product $c:C_{\mathbf Q}\to G$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

For a simple root $a\in\Delta$, put $n_a=p_a(1)p_{-a}(-1)p_a(1)$ and $s_a(m)=m-\langle m,a^\vee\rangle a$. Then $n_a$ normalizes $T_{\mathbf Q}$ and acts on it by the monomial automorphism $s_a$, and $n_a^2=a^\vee(-1)$. Use the integral reorderings to write a point of $C$ in the form
$$\left(\prod_{\beta\in\Phi^+\setminus\{a\}}p_{-\beta}(z_{-\beta})\right)p_{-a}(v)\,t\,p_a(u)\left(\prod_{\beta\in\Phi^+\setminus\{a\}}p_\beta(z_\beta)\right),$$
where each displayed $p$ over $\mathbf Z$ means the corresponding coordinate axis in its one-sign group, not multiplication in an ambient integral group. Let $V_a\subset C$ be the principal open defined in these coordinates by $d_a=1+vu\chi_a(t)$ invertible. There is a morphism $F_a:V_a\to C$ extending $c^{-1}\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)c$. Its torus restriction is $s_a$, and each root-axis restriction is $z\mapsto\epsilon_{a,\beta}z$ onto the $s_a\beta$ axis, using the signs in [lem-sfb-rational-chevalley-one-sign-integrality]. In particular $F_a(e)=e$.

Here is an additional coordinate-support assertion. For a positive system $P=w(\Phi^+)$, where $w$ is any product of root reflections, let $C_P\subset C$ be the closed coordinate subscheme with torus coordinate $1$ and coordinates outside $P$ zero. These equations can be imposed using any ordering separately on the negative and positive factors, giving the same closed subscheme. One has $C_P\subset V_a$, and $F_a$ restricts to an isomorphism of schemes $C_P\simeq C_{s_aP}$. No group structure on $C_P$ when $P$ has mixed signs, and no ambient integral reductive group, is assumed. Empty roots give no assertions indexed by $a$.

proof.text: Work only with the given rational group and the two integral one-sign groups. Apply [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] over $\mathbf Q$, with pinning $dp_a(1)$ for $a\in\Delta$. For the rank-one check, [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer] gives the reductive centralizer with roots $\{a,-a\}$ and full torus $T_{\mathbf Q}$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model] over the nonzero Noetherian field $\mathbf Q$ to this centralizer. Its model has a central split torus and matrix factor $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ or $\operatorname{GL}_2$, with root character the ratio of diagonal entries. The opposite parameters in [lem-sfb-rational-chevalley-one-sign-integrality] are the linked parameters: the displayed Gauss identity is the linked rank-one normalization (in the rank-one matrix coordinates an opposite parameter is lower-unitriangular with entry $kv$; the torus factor in the upper/lower product is $a^\vee(1+kuv)$, so comparison with $a^\vee(1+uv)$ forces $k=1$: applying $a$ and comparing the $uv$ coefficient gives $2k=2$ in $\mathbf Q$). Thus the Weyl-calculus statement applies to exactly $n_a=p_a(1)p_{-a}(-1)p_a(1)$: it normalizes $T_{\mathbf Q}$, acts by $s_a$, and $n_a^2=a^\vee(-1)$. The one-sign input gives its signed action on every root parameter. In particular it interchanges $p_a,p_{-a}$ by negation. Also $s_a$ preserves $\Phi^+\setminus\{a\}$: in the simple-root coordinates a positive root other than $a$ has some positive coefficient away from $a$, unchanged by $s_a$; since every root has coefficients of one sign, its reflected root remains positive. Applying the involution twice gives a permutation of this set.

proof.text: Use the integral reordering isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-rational-chevalley-one-sign-integrality] to put $p_{-a}(v)$ last in $E_-$ and $p_a(u)$ first in $E_+$. Denote the products of all other negative and positive axes by $L$ and $R$, so the rational product is $Lp_{-a}(v)t p_a(u)R$. Define $L'$ and $R'$ integrally by replacing, in these same ordered lists, each $p_\beta(z)$ by $p_{s_a\beta}(\epsilon_{a,\beta}z)$ and multiplying in the corresponding one-sign group. The preceding root permutation ensures that $L'$ is a product of negative axes and $R'$ a product of positive axes. These definitions use polynomial one-sign multiplication, never multiplication in an integral ambient group.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 6.3.8, equation (6.3.4), printed pp.220--222; support refinement by agent using the closed-root-set assertion of the cited Weyl-calculus node. No SGA source is used.

proof.text:
Put $q=\chi_a(t)$ and $t'=D_{\mathbf Z}(s_a)(t)$. The diagonalizable-group definition gives $\chi_{-a}(t')=q$ and $\chi_a(t')=q^{-1}$. Conjugating the middle three rational factors by $n_a$ gives
$$p_a(-v)t'p_{-a}(-u)=p_a(-v)p_{-a}(-uq)t'.$$
Apply the given rank-one Gauss identity with arguments $-v,-uq$. Its denominator is precisely $d=1+vuq$. Moving the resulting positive factor past $t'$ gives
$$p_{-a}(-uq/d)\,a^\vee(d)t'\,p_a(-vq/d).$$
Indeed $p_a(-v/d)t'=t'p_a(-vq/d)$. Hence define on $V_a=D(d)$
$$F_a(L,v,t,u,R)=\bigl(L' p_{-a}(-uq/d),\ a^\vee(d)t',\ p_a(-vq/d)R'\bigr),$$
where the first and third products are in $E_-$ and $E_+$. Every coordinate belongs to the localized coordinate ring: one-sign laws are integral polynomials, $q$ is a Laurent monomial, and for $m\in M$ the torus coordinate pulls back to $d^{\langle m,a^\vee\rangle}\chi_{s_am}(t)$. Thus these formulas define a scheme morphism over $\mathbf Z$ and reproduce $c^{-1}\operatorname{Ad}(n_a)c$ on its whole rational domain.

proof.text: On $T$ one has $u=v=0$, $L=R=1$, $d=1$, and the formula is $t\mapsto t'$. On either simple-root axis, $t=1$ and one of $u,v$ is zero, so the formula sends $p_a(u)$ to $p_{-a}(-u)$ and $p_{-a}(v)$ to $p_a(-v)$. On every other root axis $u=v=0$, and the formula is the prescribed signed axis of $L'$ or $R'$. All these axes and $T$ are contained in $V_a$ because $d=1$ there. Setting every root coordinate to zero and $t=1$ also proves $F_a(e)=e$.

proof.text: We first justify the ordering independence required to define $C_P$. A positive system $P=w\Phi^+$ is closed under nonempty sums which are roots, and has no opposite pair. This follows by applying $w^{-1}$ and adding nonnegative simple-root coefficients. The same is true of $P\cap\Phi^+$ and $P\cap(-\Phi^+)$. The closed-root-set assertion of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], applied over $\mathbf Q$, says that the product of the rational root groups in either intersection, in any enumeration, is the same subgroup scheme. Therefore each integral one-sign reordering map sends its coordinate subspace supported on that intersection into the identically supported coordinate subspace for the other ordering: the coordinates required to vanish are integral polynomials which vanish over $\mathbf Q$, hence are zero in $\mathbf Z[z_\beta]$. Apply the same argument to the inverse reordering map. This proves equality of the resulting closed subschemes over $\mathbf Z$, including after nonreduced base change. It also proves $C_P$ is a product of the axes indexed by $P$, with torus coordinate $1$, and so has torsion-free polynomial coordinate ring.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 6.3.8, equation (6.3.4), printed pp.220--222; support refinement by agent using the closed-root-set assertion of the cited Weyl-calculus node. No SGA source is used.

proof.text: In the reordered coordinates defining $V_a$, a positive system contains exactly one of $a,-a$. Consequently either $u=0$ or $v=0$ identically on $C_P$, and $q=1$, so $d=1$ as a function on this closed scheme. This proves $C_P\subset V_a$ scheme-theoretically. On it the middle output torus factor $a^\vee(d)t'$ is $1$. To check all remaining support equations, apply the closed-root-set theorem of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] over $\mathbf Q$ to $P$ and $s_aP$. It identifies $(C_P)_{\mathbf Q}$, by multiplication with negative factors before positive ones, with $U_P$; any such ordering is allowed. Signed conjugation sends each of its factors to its reflected root subgroup, hence sends $U_P$ to $U_{s_aP}$. The latter subgroup is the image of $(C_{s_aP})_{\mathbf Q}$ with its analogous negative-before-positive ordering. Uniqueness of coordinates in the assumed open immersion $c$ now implies every forbidden output coordinate of $F_a|C_P$ is zero over $\mathbf Q$. Each is a polynomial over $\mathbf Z$ (the denominator is $1$ here), so torsion-freeness makes it zero integrally. Thus $F_a$ factors through $C_{s_aP}$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 6.3.8, equation (6.3.4), printed pp.220--222; support refinement by agent using the closed-root-set assertion of the cited Weyl-calculus node. No SGA source is used.

proof.text: Apply the preceding support argument also to $s_aP$. The two restrictions can therefore be composed alternately four times. Over $\mathbf Q$ this fourth iterate is conjugation by $n_a^4=1$, since $n_a^2=a^\vee(-1)$ and $a^\vee$ is a group homomorphism. Both the fourth iterate and the identity have integral polynomial coordinates on $C_P$, so equality over $\mathbf Q$ implies equality over $\mathbf Z$ coefficient by coefficient; likewise on $C_{s_aP}$. The triple iterate starting at $C_{s_aP}$ is therefore a two-sided inverse to $F_a:C_P\to C_{s_aP}$. This proves the requested scheme isomorphism. The argument has not equipped a mixed-sign $C_P$ with a group law. In rank zero there is no $a$, so every assertion indexed by a simple root is vacuous.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-e2beffc4a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 6.3.8 and its proof, printed pp.220-222, from the PDF at the URL in the source field. Step 3's formula p_{-a}(-uq/d)·a^∨(d)t'·p_a(-vq/d) on D(1+vuq) is exactly Conrad's display, with x0=v and x=u. Statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. This is a first split of an unsplit node, not a 2026-10-21 re-split.

Step 1: I checked the linked parameters in SL2 directly. Matching the Gauss torus factor a^∨(1+cc'uv) with the one-sign node's a^∨(1+uv) forces cc'=1, so n_a=[[0,c],[-1/c,0]] and n_a^2=-I=a^∨(-1). Uniqueness of the linked generator in the Weyl-calculus node then gives Y=dp_{-a}(1). The hypotheses of the centralizer and local matrix-model nodes hold over Q. The fact that n_a sends p_{-a}(z) to p_a(-z) is not stated but follows in one line from n_a^2=a^∨(-1).

Steps 2-4: I checked the substitutions t'p_{-a}(-u)=p_{-a}(-uq)t', with χ_{-a}(t')=q and χ_a(t')=q^{-1}, and the torus pullback d^{⟨m,a^∨⟩}χ_{s_a m}(t), which is a unit on D(d). All coordinates are integral after inverting d.

Step 5: positive systems and their intersections with ±Φ^+ are closed and contain no opposite pair. The closed-root-set clause over Q then forces the forbidden coordinates to vanish in Q[z], hence in Z[z], in both directions. This is an equality of closed subschemes.

Step 6: d=1 on C_P. n_a carries U_P onto U_{s_aP}, the open immersion c is a monomorphism, and the coordinate ring is torsion-free, so F_a sends C_P into C_{s_aP}.

Step 7: n_a^4=1 gives F^4=id integrally, so F^3 is a two-sided inverse.

Edge cases checked: rank 0, SL2 with P={a} and P={-a}, characteristic 2 and nonreduced bases.

No duplicates: lem-sfb-simple-root-weyl-transport, lem-sfb-integral-chevalley-weyl-atlas and lem-sfb-rank-two-root-coordinate-classification state different results, and the remaining hits are nodes that cite this item.
